contributions.title: Fix metrics collection inaccuracies and add metrics tests
contributions.bodyHTML:
## Summary

Fixes several inaccuracies in the Prometheus metrics and adds a metrics test suite.

- **Respawn overlap:** during a graceful respawn (lifetime/RSS) the old and new worker both report to the same slot, so `worker="N"` series flip between old and new values and Prometheus sees repeated counter resets. Reports now carry the worker's birth timestamp and the aggregator ignores reports from an older worker.
- **Stale data after crash:** a crashed worker's last snapshot stayed exported until its replacement's first report. The slot is now cleared (`MetricsAggregator.clear`) before respawn.
- **`workers_respawns_for_err`:** was incremented by 1 per crash cycle regardless of how many workers crashed; now counts each worker.
- **`blocking_busy_cumulative`:** in GIL builds it included GIL re-acquire wait (already reported in `py_wait_cumulative`); now matches the free-threaded build semantics.
- **`blocking_queue`:** was incremented after `send`, so a consumer could decrement first and scrapes could observe `-1`.
- **Exposition format:** output now ends with a newline and uses `text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8`.

Note: `ipc::Message::Metrics` now carries the birth timestamp; parent and workers always run the same binary, so there's no compatibility concern.

## Tests

New `tests/test_metrics.py` (10 tests, ~35s) running real servers with metrics enabled:

- exposition format + all metrics present per worker (asgi/rsgi/wsgi)
- request/connection counting (asgi/rsgi/wsgi)
- `blocking_queue` never negative under concurrent WSGI load
- respawn overlap never re-exposes the old worker's values (RSS-forced respawn)
- crashed worker series is cleared then restored
- simultaneous crashes counted per worker (in-process `_serve_loop` test)

Verified the format, respawn, crash and respawn-count tests fail against the pre-fix code. Windows is skipped (metrics unavailable); respawn/crash tests are skipped on free-threaded builds.

`make lint` clean; full suite: 185 passed, 4 skipped locally (macOS, CPython 3.12).

contributions.title: feat: migrate WeTTY server to Rust (axum + tower + socketioxide) with napi-rs Node.js bridge
contributions.bodyHTML:
Replaces the Express/Socket.IO server with a Rust crate while keeping the TypeScript browser client and CLI entry point untouched. A napi-rs native addon maintains a backward-compatible `start()` / `decorateServerWithSsh()` API. `mise` manages the mixed Rust + Node.js toolchain.

## Rust crate (`crates/wetty-server/`)

- **`app.rs`** — axum `Router` with tower middleware: `SecurityLayer` (CSP/X-Frame-Options), `CompressionLayer`, `ServeDir`, `TraceLayer`, prometheus `/metrics` route
- **`socket.rs`** — socketioxide connection handler wiring PTY lifecycle to Socket.IO events
- **`pty.rs`** — portable-pty spawner bridged to tokio channels; uses `rt.enter()` so `tokio::spawn` works correctly from OS threads
- **`flowcontrol.rs`** — port of `TinyBuffer` (2 ms / 512 KiB flush) + `FlowControlServer` low/high watermark
- **`command.rs`** — SSH command builder mirroring `src/server/command/`
- **`ssl.rs`** — rustls TLS config (ring backend); supports cert/key path and Unix socket binding
- **`lib.rs`** — napi bindings behind optional `node-binding` feature so `cargo test` links without Node.js

## TypeScript shim

`src/server.ts` becomes a thin wrapper — same exported signatures, delegates to the `.node` addon:

```ts
import addon from '../build/wetty_server.node';
export const start: typeof addon.start = addon.start;
export const decorateServerWithSsh: typeof addon.decorateServerWithSsh = addon.decorateServerWithSsh;
```

**Breaking:** return type changes from `Promise<SocketIO.Server>` to `Promise<ServerHandle>`. Callers that interact with the returned server instance will need to adapt.

## Toolchain & build

- **`.mise.toml`** — pins Node 22, Rust 1.96.0, pnpm 9.4.0; defines `build`, `test`, `lint`, `check:rust` tasks
- **`scripts/copy-addon.sh`** — single source of truth for copying `.so`/`.dylib`/`.dll` → `build/wetty_server.node`; referenced by mise, `build.js`, and the `build:rust` npm script
- **CI** — replaced `actions/setup-node` + `pnpm/action-setup` with `jdx/mise-action@v2`; added `cargo test` step

## Tests

- 48 Rust unit tests across all modules
- 10 HTTP integration tests (`tests/app_test.rs`) — routes, security headers, redirect behaviour
- 3 TLS integration tests (`tests/ssl_test.rs`)
- `src/server.spec.ts` — TypeScript smoke tests for the shim

contributions.title: feat!: OpenTelemetry metric names, busy time in seconds, one runtime sampler per process
contributions.bodyHTML:
## What

All metrics follow OpenTelemetry naming: dotted names, no unit or `_total` in the name, semantic convention names where they exist. Prometheus with recommended naming adds the suffixes back (`process.cpu.time` → `process_cpu_time_seconds_total`).

- **Process metrics** use the semantic conventions: `process.cpu.time{cpu.mode=user|system}` (split with `getrusage` on Unix), `process.memory.usage`, `process.memory.virtual`, `process.unix.file_descriptor.count` (`process.windows.handle.count` on Windows), `process.thread.count`, `process.uptime`. Two limits not in the conventions, named in their style: `process.memory.virtual.limit`, `process.unix.file_descriptor.limit`.
- **Runtime metrics** are named `tokio.runtime.*` in the same style.
- **Units**: seconds, bytes, 0–1 ratios and counts, everywhere. Integer counters (`process.cpu.time`, `tokio.runtime.worker.busy.time`) keep an exact total and record whole seconds; the error is at most 1 s per `rate()` window.
- **One runtime sampler per process**: `export_runtime_metrics()` returns `None` while one is running, since a second would double-count or overwrite the counters and the metrics have no runtime label. A new one can start once the first stops.
- Tests fail if a process or runtime metric has no description or isn't named in its OpenTelemetry namespace.

## Breaking (against 0.2.2)

Process metrics, released in 0.2.2:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `process_cpu_seconds_total` | `process.cpu.time{cpu.mode}` |
| `process_resident_memory_bytes` | `process.memory.usage` |
| `process_virtual_memory_bytes` | `process.memory.virtual` |
| `process_virtual_memory_max_bytes` | `process.memory.virtual.limit` |
| `process_open_fds` | `process.unix.file_descriptor.count` / `process.windows.handle.count` |
| `process_max_fds` | `process.unix.file_descriptor.limit` |
| `process_threads` | `process.thread.count` |
| `process_start_time_seconds` | `process.uptime` (seconds since start) |

Runtime metrics:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `tokio_runtime_workers` | `tokio.runtime.worker.count` |
| `tokio_runtime_live_tasks` | `tokio.runtime.task.count` |
| `tokio_runtime_global_queue_depth` | `tokio.runtime.global_queue.depth` |
| `tokio_runtime_worker_busy_ratio` (`_max`, `_min`) | `tokio.runtime.worker.utilization` (`.max`, `.min`) |
| `tokio_runtime_worker_busy_microseconds_total` (µs) | `tokio.runtime.worker.busy.time` (**seconds**) |
| `tokio_runtime_worker_parks_total` | `tokio.runtime.worker.parks` |
| `tokio_runtime_poll_duration_mean_seconds` (`_max_`) | `tokio.runtime.poll.duration.mean` (`.max`) |
| `tokio_runtime_polls_total`, `_steals_total` | `tokio.runtime.worker.polls`, `.steals` |
| `tokio_runtime_local_queue_depth` (`_max`) | `tokio.runtime.local_queue.depth` (`.max`) |
| `tokio_runtime_blocking_threads` (`_idle`) | `tokio.runtime.blocking.thread.count` (`.idle.count`) |
| `tokio_runtime_blocking_queue_depth` | `tokio.runtime.blocking.queue.depth` |

`export_runtime_metrics()` returns `Option<JoinHandle<()>>` instead of `JoinHandle<()>`.

Dashboards and alerts on the old names need updating.

## Testing

- `cargo test --locked --all-features`, with and without `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"`
- `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets`: clean
- `prek run --all-files`: passes

contributions.title: fix: redact credential query names that are percent-encoded
contributions.bodyHTML:
## Problem

Query parameter names were matched as sent, so a credential whose name is percent-encoded got past redaction. `?access%5Ftoken=secret&page=2` recorded `secret` in the server span's `url.query`, and the client's `url.full` had the same gap. `+` as a space and mixed-case escapes such as `ACCESS%5fTOKEN` had the same problem.

## Change

- Each parameter name is decoded before matching: `%XX` is that byte and `+` is a space. The built-in names and the names added through `SpanDecorator::SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS` or `OtelClientTraceLayer::with_redacted_query_keys` are all matched this way, still without regard to case.
- The output keeps each name as it was sent, and only the value becomes `REDACTED`.
- A name is decoded only when it contains `%` or `+`, so the common case still borrows and doesn't allocate.
- An escape that isn't two hex digits, or a decoded result that isn't UTF-8, doesn't match. Such a name can't be one of the credential names, so nothing panics.

## Behaviour changes

- Credential names are redacted in encoded form too, on the server span and in the client's `url.full`.
- No public API changes.

## Tests

- Unit (`src/request.rs`): `access%5Ftoken`, `ACCESS%5fTOKEN`, `%61ccess_token`, a user-added name written encoded, `+` as a space, a decoded name that isn't a credential left alone, and invalid escapes (`%zz`, `%5`, `%`, `%FF`, `%2`) that don't match and don't panic.
- Server span (`tests/trace.rs`): an encoded built-in name and an encoded user-added name are redacted and kept as sent.
- Client `url.full` (`tests/trace.rs`): an encoded built-in name is redacted.
- README and rustdoc on the matching rules now say names are matched after percent-decoding.

contributions.title: feat: process metrics, tokio_unstable runtime metrics, metric descriptions
contributions.bodyHTML:
## What

- **`process-metrics` feature**: `export_process_metrics()` spawns a sampler that records the standard Prometheus process metrics every 5 seconds, via [`metrics-process`](https://crates.io/crates/metrics-process) (Linux, macOS, Windows, BSDs):
  `process_cpu_seconds_total`, `process_resident_memory_bytes`, `process_virtual_memory_bytes`, `process_virtual_memory_max_bytes`, `process_open_fds`, `process_max_fds`, `process_threads`, `process_start_time_seconds`.
- **`tokio_unstable` runtime metrics**: built with `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"`, `export_runtime_metrics()` also records
  `tokio_runtime_poll_duration_mean_seconds`, `_poll_duration_mean_max_seconds`, `_polls_total`, `_steals_total`, `_local_queue_depth`, `_local_queue_depth_max`, `_blocking_threads`, `_blocking_threads_idle`, `_blocking_queue_depth`. Without the cfg nothing changes.
- **Descriptions**: the panic counter and every `tokio_runtime_*` metric are now described with a unit. StatsD has no metadata channel, so this only shows up in Prometheus `# HELP` / OTLP.
- **CI**: a step runs the lib tests with `--cfg tokio_unstable`.

Later commits pushed here after the merge (OpenTelemetry names, busy time in seconds, one sampler per process) are in the follow-up PR.

contributions.title: fix: bound url.scheme and redact credentials in url.query
contributions.bodyHTML:
## Problem

- **Credentials in server span query strings.** `OtelTraceLayer` recorded the raw query as `url.query`, so a request with `?access_token=...` exported the credential with the span. The client layer already redacted signed-URL parameters in `url.full`, but the server side had no equivalent.
- **Unbounded `url.scheme` metric series.** `url.scheme` came from `X-Forwarded-Proto`, or from the scheme of an absolute-form request URI, verbatim. The metric label kept any value, so each distinct value sent by an unauthenticated client created a new series.
- **No way to extend the redacted names.** The built-in list is fixed, so an application whose own parameter names carry credentials couldn't have them redacted.

## Change

- `url.scheme` is `http`, `https` or `_OTHER` on server spans and metric labels, as `http.request.method` already is for methods. The bound lives in `request::scheme`, so spans and metrics agree.
- `url.query` on the server span keeps parameter names and replaces credential values with `REDACTED`. The server span and the client's `url.full` share one built-in list: `AWSAccessKeyId`, `Signature`, `sig`, `X-Goog-Signature`, `X-Amz-Signature`, `X-Amz-Credential`, `X-Amz-Security-Token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token`, `token`, `api_key` and `client_secret`. Names match case-insensitively. A query with nothing to redact is borrowed, so the common case doesn't allocate.

### Adding names to redact

Both hooks extend the built-in list and never replace it.

- **Server:** `SpanDecorator::SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS`, an associated const that defaults to empty.

  ```rust
  impl SpanDecorator for ApiKeyDecorator {
      const SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS: &'static [&'static str] = &["x-api-key"];
  }
  let layer = OtelTraceLayer::<ApiKeyDecorator>::default();
  ```

- **Client:** `OtelClientTraceLayer::with_redacted_query_keys(keys: &'static [&'static str]) -> RedactingClientTraceLayer`. `OtelClientTraceLayer` is unchanged, so `.layer(OtelClientTraceLayer)` still compiles. The new layer type is what carries the names.

  ```rust
  let layer = OtelClientTraceLayer::with_redacted_query_keys(&["x-api-key"]);
  ```

Tests cover both hooks, the built-in list still applying with extras present, and case-insensitive matching.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- `url.scheme` values other than `http` and `https` now appear as `_OTHER`, on spans and metrics.
- The client's `url.full` redacts more parameter names than before.
- The only public additions are `SpanDecorator::SENSITIVE_QUERY_KEYS`, `OtelClientTraceLayer::with_redacted_query_keys` and the `RedactingClientTraceLayer` type. Version and CHANGELOG are untouched; release-please generates the CHANGELOG from commits.

## Not included

- No switch to stop recording the query entirely. Redaction removes credential values; an opt-out would be a further hook for one attribute.
- Parameter names are matched as sent. A percent-encoded name such as `access%5Ftoken` isn't decoded before matching.

contributions.title: perf!: fewer allocations per request; leave span status unset on success
contributions.bodyHTML:
Measured with the new `benches/layers.rs` (criterion; one request through each layer with a Prometheus recorder and an OpenTelemetry tracer installed):

| Benchmark | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| server: no layers | 543 ns | 538 ns | none |
| server: `HttpMetricsLayer` | 2.69 µs | 2.32 µs | −14% |
| server: `OtelTraceLayer` | 2.76 µs | 2.74 µs | none |
| client: metrics and trace | 3.10 µs | 2.93 µs | −7% |
| messaging: process | 1.68 µs | 1.58 µs | −17% |

Changes:
- Metric label values are static for known values (common status codes, ports 80/443, schemes, well-known messaging systems, default operation names), and `Arc`-backed for computed ones (route, host, `MetricLabels`). Each metric copies the labels, and copies are now pointer or refcount copies, not string allocations.
- Label vectors are allocated once with room for the outcome labels.
- `url.full` is built in one allocation.
- **Breaking:** `SpanDecorator::on_response` no longer takes the span's `opentelemetry::Context`. Call `span.context()` when needed; `PropagatingSpanDecorator` does.
- **Fix:** `mark_server_errors` leaves the span status unset on success instead of setting `OK`, as the conventions ask of instrumentation, and sets `error.type` on `5xx`.

BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE
perf: cheaper metric labels: static for known values, shared for computed ones
feat!: SpanDecorator::on_response no longer takes the span's context; call span.context() when needed
fix: leave HTTP server span status unset on success, and set error.type on 5xx
END_COMMIT_OVERRIDE

contributions.title: perf: inline small hot-path helpers and builder methods
contributions.bodyHTML:
The layers' generic code (`Service::call`, the futures, the bodies) is compiled in the user's crate. Calls from it into this crate's non-generic helpers cross a crate boundary, and can't be inlined without `#[inline]` or LTO.

- `#[inline]` on the small per-request helpers: header, host and port parsing, method and version names, health-check matching, label building, and `Side::is_error`.
- `#[inline]` on the tiny public builders and accessors: the `MessagingSpan` setters, `MessagingOperation::as_str`/`span_kind`, `with_names`, `with_host_label`, and `MetricNames::durations`/`body_sizes`.
- `server.port` labels for 80 and 443 are static strings, not a fresh allocation per request.

No behaviour change.

contributions.title: feat: OpenTelemetry messaging metrics and MessagingSpan::run
contributions.bodyHTML:
With `messaging` and `metrics` both on:

- `MessageTraceLayer` records `messaging.process.duration` and `messaging.client.consumed.messages` per message.
- New `MessagingSpan::run(|span| future)`: runs an operation inside its span, marks failures on it, and records `messaging.client.operation.duration`, plus `messaging.client.sent.messages` for `send`.
- Labels follow the conventions: system, operation name and type, destination (the template when set), consumer group, server address and port, and `error.type` on failure.
- A `receive` through `run` records its duration but not consumed messages, so messages aren't counted twice.

Without `metrics`, `run` still traces and marks errors.
